sources.version: BMC Evolutionary Biology 15, article 56; version of record published 2015-04-08
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study site and subjects; Results, Sample size and Context-specific call variants; Discussion; Conclusion

sources.scope: Field acoustic study of free-ranging lar gibbons in natural forest at Mo Singto, Khao Yai National Park, Thailand. Only paraphrased article text findings are used; no recordings, figures or third-party material are reused.

gaps: No morphology evidence was assessed in this batch.
Reproduction, development, lifespan and other life-history traits have not been assessed.

claims.text: Researchers extracted 462 close-range ‘hoo’ calls from 14 males and 11 females across nine contexts. In the adequately sampled contexts included in the main analyses, acoustic parameters varied by context in both sexes; for example, raptor-context calls had lower peak and low frequencies than duet calls. The authors note that playback tests are needed to determine whether recipients discriminate these variants.
claims.locator: Results, Sample size and Context-specific call variants; Discussion; Conclusion
claims.placeTimeScope: Mo Singto, Khao Yai National Park, northeastern Thailand; observations totalled 117 field days and approximately 600 hours. Analysis used 462 calls from nine contexts; alert, separation and snake contexts had too few samples for the main analyses.
claims.lifeStatus: Free-ranging wild adult male and female gibbons; no captive animals are included.

gaps: The study is limited to one field site and a finite call sample; it does not establish geographic or population-wide variation, and receiver comprehension was not tested by playback.
No phylogenetic or evolutionary evidence was assessed.
The study site is not a species-wide range inventory or locality history.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No threat status, population trend or range-wide conservation assessment was assessed.

reasons: Only one bounded field acoustic study was assessed; six facets remain not-assessed.
Evidence is limited to sampled callers, contexts and one Thai study site; this is not a systematic review or complete species account.
No independent expert review has been completed.
